text.p: McKesson Corp said Wednesday its FoxMeyer business diluted fourth quarter earnings by about $0.05 a share and earnings for the fiscal year by $0.10 a share.

McKesson said it expects the acquisition will be breakeven in April and accretive to earnings in fiscal 1998. McKesson completed the acquisition of FoxMeyer, the fourth-largest U.S. distributor of pharmaceuticals, in November 1996.

"We are very pleased with both the sales retention and the pace of consolidation of the FoxMeyer acquisition, in which we undertook to service a large number of new customers and to drive cost efficiencies," said Chief Financial Officer Richard Hawkins.

"Our aggressive integration programs, including the closure of seven distribution centers through March, should enable the acquisition to reach breakeven in April and be accretive to earnings in fiscal 1998."
McKesson reported fourth quarter diluted operating earnings of $0.81 a share on revenues of $4 billion, up from $0.77 a share on revenues of $2.6 billion in the year-ago period.
